study type: secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial
outcome: noninfectious wound complications (seroma, hematoma, local cellulitis, other noninfectious wound breakdown)
cohort: Women with singleton pregnancies >=24 weeks who were undergoing nonelective cesarean delivery.
finding: Adding azithromycin to usual antibiotic prophylaxis for nonelective cesarean delivery did not significantly reduce the risk of postcesarean noninfectious wound complications.
mod_finding: The primary finding concerns post-cesarean noninfectious wound complications, directly relating to the mode of birth being a nonelective cesarean delivery.
